flex

Your number is your identity.

A unique number and an NFC object that opens it. One tap — nothing to install.

The problem

Paper is printed once.
Everything else changes.

A card is out of date the day it is printed

A new job, a new number, a new company — and the box in the drawer is wrong. People hand them over anyway.

A menu is a photograph of last month's prices

A cafe reprints, or crosses lines out with a pen. The dish that ran out at lunch is still on every table.

A table cannot ask for anything

A guest raises a hand and waits for someone to look. The cafe never learns which tables waited, or for how long.

The solution

One tap, and the page opens.

1

The number

Three letters and three digits — MYN042 — become an address, and it is yours for life.

2

The object

A card, a ring, a bracelet, or a tag on a table. An NFC chip and a QR code inside.

3

The page

The guest taps their own phone and it opens in their own language. Nobody installs anything.

flex.com.uz3
Design

One number, many faces.

The owner picks the card design, and every one of them is drawn by us rather than borrowed. A low serial number cannot be reproduced at all — which is the one thing on the card that is genuinely scarce.

At the entry band of 149,000 UZS and nothing above it — a hotel or a larger restaurant pays twice that. Devices and personal numbers are not counted here at all. These are venue counts, not a market size.

flex.com.uz9
Why now

Three things are true at once.

The phones are ready

Every phone sold in recent years reads NFC, and after 2020 a QR code on a table needs no explaining to anyone.

Service is the battleground

Cafes and hotels no longer compete on price alone. How fast somebody answers a table is a thing guests notice.

The rails exist

Payme and bank transfer make a monthly subscription collectable from a business — what turns this from a gadget into revenue.
